pages.name: csdlc
pages.summary: operate the authenticated C-SDLC v3 lifecycle

SYNOPSIS.code:
csdlc --help
csdlc --contract
csdlc COMMAND --describe
csdlc COMMAND --help
man csdlc-COMMAND
man csdlc-requests
man csdlc-workflow

DESCRIPTION: C-SDLC v3 is the current lifecycle authority after #505 / PR #591 only when canonical origin/main selector, authenticated native receipt, terminal reconciliation and Git objects validate. Missing or stale proof suspends authority. A printed plan, a construction report, an install, or a boolean in a request cannot grant it.

This suite documents the committed native command contract. It includes all help-listed commands plus the supported rollback alias and github-issue create/close forms. The active simplification issues may change future behavior; rerun command/option parity after integration. Historical v1 wrappers and retained v2 binaries are not routine operational routes.

Discovery is compiled from the current command manifest: --contract returns the raw full descriptor manifest and COMMAND --describe returns the raw command descriptor, including input contract, effect class and result schema. These global discovery forms do not execute the route and are separate from owner-specific parser options. The selected binary must support this contract; source or isolated candidate validation does not prove that the active installation has been upgraded.

INSTALLATION.code:
bash adl/tools/install_owner_binaries.sh --bin csdlc
export PATH="$PWD/.adl/bin/native-v3:$PATH"
export MANPATH="$PWD/.adl/bin/native-v3/share/man:${MANPATH:-}"
man csdlc
man csdlc-finish

INSTALLATION: The owner installer installs the manual under STABLE_BIN_DIR/share/man/man1 and prints discovery instructions; it does not edit shell startup files or global system directories. Set PATH and MANPATH in your own shell as above. The trailing MANPATH colon retains system manual paths on macOS and Linux. --stable-bin-dir changes the binary and manual prefix together. A docs-only refresh does not rebuild or replace an unchanged binary.

The native csdlc install command is an issue-bound proof/install route with a separate .adl/bin/csdlc destination and explicit approval. It is not the owner installer or manual installer. See csdlc-install(1).
LIFECYCLE: Prepare issue-specific SIP -> STP -> SPP -> VPP -> SRP -> SOR using the active template registry. Native issue/edit/validate/doctor prepare a local issue; bind creates the registered execution worktree. Implement and validate proportionally, obtain independent exact-head review, and check native review before publication. Native publish validates publication admission; github-pr executes the actual create/update/ready/merge transport. Finish observes merged PR plus closed issue and may persist terminal records; clean independently previews and removes only the exact eligible registered checkout.

Use csdlc-workflow(1) for the complete operator sequence. A successful command exit is not sufficient: inspect operational_authority, result status/findings, exact issue/head and mutation flags. A ready model-only plan is not executed work.
CONVENTIONS: --help and -h are standalone help arguments, not global options mixed into another invocation. There is no --version, --json, --quiet, --root or global --repo option. JSON is the machine output format; do not use retired wrapper flags. Paths to CLI input files are resolved by the invoking process. Typed relative path fields use the root declared by their owning contract; consult csdlc-requests(1).

Local commands accept --repo-root for discovery and --v3-state-root for retained construction storage. Ordinary operations should run from clean primary main during preparation, then from the native-bound issue checkout. Do not use alternate roots to bypass ownership. Exact SHA means the full 40-hex Git revision. Local lifecycle digests and remote canonical selector digests are different values.

Machine command results preserve legacy owner payload fields and add /envelope with schema csdlc.v3.command_result.v1. Successful --contract and COMMAND --describe responses return their descriptor directly; help remains text. Process outcome, lifecycle status, authority and effects are separate. A successful exit or ready report does not prove mutation, publication or terminal delivery. Unknown effects and unreported evidence invalidation are not no-effect evidence; inspect owner results and durable receipts.
CREDENTIALS: Select credential names, never credential values, in credential_names or --credential-name. The default simple-issue name is GITHUB_TOKEN. The current native resolver first reads the selected environment variable; if absent, GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN may use the explicitly set ADL_GITHUB_TOKEN_FILE. A set-but-empty variable fails; it does not fall back. Other credential names require their corresponding environment variable.

For the operator-approved token file use ADL_GITHUB_TOKEN_FILE="$HOME/keys/github.token" only on commands needing GitHub access. Do not print or retain its contents. This committed native resolver requires the explicit file variable; it does not automatically discover a default file. Invalid credentials, unsafe token characters or unavailable authentication fail closed. Child processes receive scoped credentials and sanitized environments. Retained curl transport uses a private temporary config and removes the file; do not mistake temporary file cleanup for a completely write-free observation.
EXIT STATUS: 0 means the command returned a report (or help); some planning reports still contain blocked findings. 2 means usage, parsing, guard, transport or execution failure. Read the structured status as well as the process exit status.

Successful JSON reports go to stdout. Current proof/release-preflight blocked reports also go to stdout with a short diagnostic on stderr. Other current failures may serialize findings on stderr with a csdlc prefix. Do not assume all errors are JSON stdout. The v3 CLI does not implement ADL_OBSERVABILITY_STDERR or ADL_OBSERVABILITY_LOG overrides; this manual claims no such compatibility mode.
FILES: Primary local preparation: resolved Git metadata csdlc-v3/local/issues/ISSUE/{index.json,values/,cards/}. In an ordinary primary checkout this is .git/csdlc-v3/local. Linked issue state: .csdlc/issues/ISSUE/{index.json,values/,cards/}. Local locks and transactions live beneath that resolved local state root, including transactions/ISSUE.json and completed transaction records.

Remote intents, recovery and mutation receipts live beneath resolved common Git metadata csdlc-v3/remote/. Merge intent/reconciliation lives in remote/merges/. Temporary private transport inputs live under resolved Git runtime metadata. Do not delete uncertain intent, locks, journals, stages or backup records as a recovery shortcut.

Terminal state is LOCAL_ROOT/v3/issues/ISSUE/terminal.json and LOCAL_ROOT/evidence/ISSUE/terminal-receipt.json. LOCAL_ROOT is resolved Git metadata csdlc-v3/local on primary and .csdlc in linked checkout. Use paths returned by the native result and preserve exact topology. Proof artifacts are issue-scoped .csdlc/evidence/ISSUE in the invoking bound checkout.
DIAGNOSTICS: authority missing/stale: inspect canonical origin/main selector, native receipt and referenced Git objects, then route authority repair through its owner. Do not switch to v2 or raw GitHub writes.
stale_lifecycle_digest: reread actual native index/generation, compare the intended field edits, refresh the request from that state, and validate. Never copy an unrelated issue digest.
github_credential_missing or credential resolution failed: set the approved credential source explicitly and retry the same read. Never put the token into JSON or argv.
review stale/head mismatch: verify actual branch HEAD, rerun affected proof and independent review at that head, refresh the typed receipt and native review. Do not relabel an old receipt.

incorrect checkout topology/invalid_operational_roots: inspect git status --short --branch and git worktree list --porcelain. Return to the exact registered branch and native-bound checkout; preserve existing work. Do not hand-edit index binding or register fake worktrees.

finish without --observe-github: a caller-provided public_adapter_receipt is not authentication. Use native finish --observe-github with numeric PR, expected head and closing mode; a still-open issue or unmerged PR remains blocked.

uncertain remote mutation/reconciliation: preserve request and intent bytes, then reissue the identical native request to reconcile authenticated remote state. Do not change IDs, delete receipts or repeat a raw write. Only explicitly supported creation/ready absence recovery may request its one-shot retry. Merge and issue-edit uncertain retries are observation-only.

Doctor, validate, eligibility, schedule and shepherd observe without creating lifecycle locks or replaying interrupted transactions. Reported recovery-required state must be handled by an explicit mutation/recovery route. Operational local routes fail closed when authority context is unavailable; only explicit local selects the non-operational construction helper. This guarantee does not make issue, edit or bind observational.
SEE ALSO: csdlc-workflow(1), csdlc-requests(1), csdlc-doctor(1), csdlc-github-pr(1), csdlc-finish(1), csdlc-clean(1). Repository policy: AGENTS.md, docs/csdlc-v3/CURRENT_AUTHORITY.md, docs/csdlc-v3/CONTRACT.md and docs/csdlc-v3/PULL_REQUEST_MERGE.md.

pages.name: csdlc-local
pages.summary: inspect retained local preparation model

SYNOPSIS.code:
csdlc local --request REQUEST --registry REGISTRY --registrations REGISTRATIONS
  [--repo-root ROOT] [--v3-state-root ROOT]
csdlc local --help

DESCRIPTION: Constructs render, dependency and bind plans from the request, active registry and registration inventory. It neither creates a GitHub issue nor binds a checkout. A proposed branch generally must have a matching registration for the retained helper plan; do not invent a registration to obtain a green result.
EFFECTS: Read-only helper; no operational authority.
Do not interpret read_only in an older report as a byte-level filesystem guarantee. See csdlc(1) for current observation guarantees, selected-binary discovery and the primary/linked path distinction.
OPTIONS: --request: Required path to a UTF-8 JSON request of the command's request family.
--registry: Required path to docs/templates/prompts/current.json; selects the active versioned templates and schemas.
--registrations: Required JSON array of actual Git worktree registrations, each {branch, worktree, primary}; refresh from live git worktree list --porcelain.
--repo-root: Explicit repository discovery root. Required by foundation/sprint; optional for local-family commands. It does not override authenticated binding guards.
--v3-state-root: Optional retained construction state root for issue/eligibility; not a primary-checkout artifact location or an ownership bypass.
--help: Show standalone help; -h is equivalent.
-h: Show standalone help; do not combine with execution options.

Reissue the exact interrupted mutating issue/bind/edit request through its native owner after checking the bound topology; do not use diagnostics as a repair command. SIMPLE FORMS.code:
csdlc github-issue create --repo OWNER/REPO --title TITLE \
  (--body BODY | --body-file PATH) --expected-head SHA \
  [--label LABEL]... [--assignee LOGIN]... [--milestone NUMBER] \
  [--credential-name NAME] [--execute]
csdlc github-issue close --repo OWNER/REPO --issue NUMBER \
  --disposition duplicate|superseded|no-op --rationale TEXT \
  (--body CURRENT_BODY | --body-file PATH) --expected-head SHA \
  [--duplicate-of NUMBER] [--credential-name NAME] [--execute]

SIMPLE FORMS: Without --execute these forms print the same typed dispatch for inspection; --expected-head is still a full exact SHA and canonical selector discovery must succeed. --body/--body-file are mutually exclusive and one is required. --label/--assignee repeat; other duplicate flags fail. --milestone, --issue and --duplicate-of are positive numeric IDs. Duplicate close requires --duplicate-of. --disposition also accepts no_op. --credential-name selects an environment name (default GITHUB_TOKEN), never a token value.

Close appends rationale and disposition to the authenticated current issue body, sets closed/not_planned, and retains the operation marker. A supplied current body containing an existing native operation marker is rejected by the current simple form; use a reviewed typed request preserving exact provenance rather than removing markers opportunistically.

issue_edit optional metadata: omitted title/body/labels/assignees/milestone preserves the corresponding remote value. labels is {operation:add|remove|replace,names:[...]}; replacement [] clears. assignees [] clears. milestone is {operation:set,number:N} or {operation:clear}. Bare null metadata fails; explicit empty body clears prose while retaining native marker. Deltas are resolved once and intent/readback binds the resolved target.

DESCRIPTION: Checks exact candidate revision, release notes bytes, gate/inventory/evidence digests and package/lockfile consistency. Gate evidence is an input, never release authorization. This route does not tag, publish or mutate GitHub. Git status inspection disables optional locks to avoid index refresh; this observation does not grant release or mutation authority.

The current route is explicitly limited to repository agent-logic/agent-design-language and version v0.92.1; other versions report unsupported_release_identity. Do not claim v0.92.2 release readiness from this older bounded checker.
OPTIONS: --request: Required path to a UTF-8 JSON request of the command's request family.
--help: Show standalone help; -h is equivalent.
-h: Show standalone help; do not combine with execution options.
REQUEST: Release preflight Request; see csdlc-requests(1) and docs/csdlc-v3/man/examples/release.json.
EFFECTS: Observation or static model only. Read findings/status, not just process exit status; no release or lifecycle activation authority is granted.

pages.name: csdlc-requests
pages.summary: native request fields, enums and digest contracts

DESCRIPTION: This is the operator-readable request field reference. Strings are JSON strings, u64 values are nonnegative JSON integers, bool values are JSON booleans, Vec values are arrays and map values are JSON objects. Optional fields may be omitted; a schema-valid shape is only the first gate. Current identity, positive issue IDs where required, authority, receipts, path confinement and operation-specific guards are still mandatory.

The checked-in examples are schema fixtures, not authenticated credentials, approvals, reviews or remote readback. Replace all illustrative IDs/paths/digests from live evidence before execution. Do not copy a fixture's true readiness flags as facts. Request JSON files have no wrapper schema field unless the named type defines one.
LOCAL CONTRACT: LocalPreparationRequest.commands uses prepare_issue, bind_worktree, edit_cards, plan_pvf, doctor, schedule, shepherd and eligibility. validate requires plan_pvf. The six card_updates keys are sip, stp, spp, vpp, srp and sor; fields come from the active registry's versioned values schemas. No hand-authored rendered cards.

Expected local digest is index.json.digest from the current native state. First issue preparation omits it; bind/edit and subsequent guarded operations use the current value. Registry version must match docs/templates/prompts/current.json. WorktreeRegistration contains actual branch without refs/heads/, normalized absolute worktree and primary boolean; detached checkouts cannot masquerade as issue branches.

schedule_readiness requires every named dimension. shepherd_routing.validation is optional observed validation status, with explicit dependency_wait, retryable_failure, repair_needed and operator_decision_needed booleans. Do not set readiness from desired outcomes.
REMOTE CONTRACT: RemoteRouteRequest.mode is closing or part_of; readback_source is github, caller or fixture, and only authenticated GitHub evidence qualifies for operational readback. review_present alone is not a review. TypedReviewReceipt.schema is csdlc.v3.typed_review_receipt.v1; repository/issue/head/reviewed_revision must match, reviewer must differ from implementer, and evidence_digest must name actual review evidence.

OperationalRemoteDispatchRequest.operation is {kind:review|publish|github_mutation,request:{...}}. review and publish nest RemoteRouteRequest; github_mutation nests GithubMutationRequest. expected_lifecycle_digest is the payload digest of canonical origin/main authority-selector bytes and exact_review_sha is current reviewed HEAD. Do not substitute the local issue digest.

GithubMutationRequest.mutation is tagged by action. issue_create requires title/body and optionally labels, assignees, milestone. issue_comment requires body. issue_edit optionally supplies title/body and explicit metadata operations documented by csdlc-github-issue(1). issue_close requires rationale/current_body/disposition (duplicate|superseded|no_op), duplicate_of for duplicate, and only not_planned for github_state_reason.

pull_request_create requires base/head/title/body and optional draft boolean. head is the actual branch name and expected_head_sha is its exact reviewed SHA. pull_request_update supplies title/body. pull_request_ready has no payload fields. pull_request_merge requires base, method merge, review_receipt_path, review_receipt_digest and operator_approval in the enclosing request. Only github-pr owns merge.

recovery may be retry_after_authenticated_absence for supported creation/ready cases; it is not generic retry permission and cannot replay merge or issue-edit writes. cutover_issue/operator_approval do not grant authority by themselves.
DIGESTS: Digest algorithms are field-specific. Artifact/terminal byte digests use BLAKE3 of the exact bytes. Remote stable payload digests use BLAKE3 over each ordered UTF-8 field followed by a NUL byte. Canonical authority selector payload digest is BLAKE3 of origin/main:csdlc-v3/operator/authority-selector.json bytes followed by NUL. Whitespace in those bytes matters.

Typed review payload field order: schema, repository, issue rendered as decimal, implementer, reviewer, reviewed_revision, expected_head_sha, evidence_digest; append NUL after each. The typed receipt file itself need not have the same byte digest. Use the supplied fixture-checked operator digest example rather than confusing SHA-256 or a file hash with this payload digest.

A native result's returned digest/receipt path is preferable to recomputing a lifecycle receipt. Never claim authentication by writing a receipt with a matching checksum; transport-derived receipts require actual native observation.
TERMINAL CONTRACT: TerminalRouteRequest.mode is closing or part_of. Ordinary finish needs numeric pull_request, expected_head_sha and closing mode plus --observe-github. terminal_state identifies the actual repository_root and exact canonical state_path/receipt_path; optional expected_state_digest binds existing terminal bytes. Omitting terminal_state performs observation without durable terminal persistence.

NoPrCloseout.disposition is retired_without_execution, duplicate, superseded, absorbed, coordination_completed or historical_disposition. It requires operator/rationale/evidence_refs and exact authenticated issue updated/closed timestamps. It is administrative disposition, not merged implementation. expected_head_sha must match the actual reconciliation checkout for this route.

CleanupRouteRequest.remove defaults false. terminal_receipt is not sufficient alone: use terminal_receipt_path and its exact BLAKE3 byte digest, then preview_receipt_digest returned by an eligible preview for removal. approved_parent/repository_root/candidate_path must be actual normalized paths; candidate must be absolute. Preserve dirty or live work.

CutoverDecisionRequest.operation is apply (default) or rollback; execute defaults false. Execution requires exact selected binary, selector, installation, rollback receipt and readiness evidence paths/digests plus explicit approval. Retained cutover configuration is not a routine startup requirement.
PROOF CONTRACT: ProofWorktreeBinding compares worktree, branch, exact_head, git_common_dir, generation and lifecycle_digest with the actual native-bound issue. evidence_root is that checkout. ProofManifest.normalization is doctor_issue_phase_v1 or route_preview_v1; command.generation is v3 (v2 is retained historical input only). provider_side_effects must be false for this bounded proof.

ShadowCommandSpec.binary_ref/request_ref/side_effect_boundary_refs are confined artifact references, argv is a literal argument array, and timeout_millis is an explicit bound. No shell expansion occurs. doctor_issue_phase_v1 normalizes a real doctor response; route_preview_v1 expects the exact typed semantic preview contract, not arbitrary help text. The current CLI has no --preview producer, so routine examples use doctor_issue_phase_v1; do not invent a successful preview invocation.

InstallPlanInput requires verified source artifact/provenance/selector references and digests. stable_destination must be truthful. executes_install true requires destination .adl/bin/csdlc, exact head and matching explicit cutover_approval_ref/digest. ShadowComparison and SoakEvidence remain historical parseable shapes; the public shadow/soak execution routes are disabled.
SPRINT AND RELEASE: SprintReadinessRequest.sprints contains SprintReadinessTarget entries. execution_mode is sequential, parallel or hybrid. child_readback_refs maps issue-number strings to retained typed issue readback files; umbrella_readback_ref identifies the umbrella readback. Paths are bounded repository references. This retained helper does not prove current native cards merely by accepting readbacks.

ReleaseRequest carries exact repository/version/candidate_sha, notes_path/notes_digest and gate_path/gate_digest. The gate schema is csdlc.v3.release_gate.v1, with repository/version/candidate_sha/notes_path/notes_digest/inventory_digest/status status must be ready_for_preflight, and evidence [{issue,path,digest}]. Evidence and inventories are versioned repository inputs, not caller release authorization.

pages.name: csdlc-workflow
pages.summary: prepare, execute, publish and reconcile one issue

PRECONDITIONS: Use an existing tracked issue, accepted prerequisites and a reviewed issue-specific plan. Check clean primary main and actual registrations; preserve another session's checkout. Commands below are templates using your own reviewed request files, not permission to mutate example IDs. Use the active installed binary by absolute path after changing checkouts.

Optional documentation helper: cargo run --quiet --manifest-path csdlc-v3/Cargo.toml --example operator_manual -- ACTION PATH. Actions selector-digest, review-digest, file-digest and registrations only read and print. It requires the pinned Rust toolchain/dependencies and is not installed as a lifecycle owner. It calls the current native public digest functions; it does not authenticate authored receipts.

1 PREPARE.code:
git status --short --branch
git worktree list --porcelain
csdlc issue --request prepare.json --registry docs/templates/prompts/current.json --registrations registrations.json
csdlc edit --request design-edit.json --registry docs/templates/prompts/current.json --registrations registrations.json
csdlc validate --request current.json --registry docs/templates/prompts/current.json --registrations registrations.json
csdlc doctor --request current.json --registry docs/templates/prompts/current.json --registrations registrations.json

1 PREPARE: Store invocation files under the resolved primary Git metadata csdlc-v3/local/invocations/ISSUE, not untracked primary artifacts. prepare.json uses LocalPreparationRequest from csdlc-requests(1), the existing issue identity and proposed approved branch/worktree, registry version from current.json, full required commands and no initial expected digest.

Native issue creates six template-based cards. Set design-edit.json.card_updates to issue-specific values from the active template field schemas using the relevant card-editor skills. Preserve SIP/STP/SPP design truth, select proportional VPP lane, and leave review/output completion unclaimed. Before each following command refresh expected_lifecycle_digest from actual LOCAL_ROOT/issues/ISSUE/index.json.digest. Readiness dimensions must reflect observed prerequisites, path ownership and budget.
Generate registrations.json from actual Git topology using the optional registrations helper. Read every returned finding. A schema-valid generic template is not an accepted design.

2 BIND.code:
csdlc bind --request current.json --registry docs/templates/prompts/current.json --registrations registrations.json
cd /absolute/approved/issue-worktree
csdlc doctor --request current.json --registry docs/templates/prompts/current.json --registrations registrations.json

2 BIND: Verify the exact native bound branch, returned worktree, phase and six cards. Refresh current.json from the worktree .csdlc/issues/ISSUE/index.json and refresh registrations after bind. Use an absolute installed binary path or configured PATH. Create the issue-bound session goal before implementation; keep root main inspection-only.
3 IMPLEMENT AND REVIEW: Implement only planned paths, execute VPP's smallest meaningful proof, update SPP if the plan changes and SOR with actual results through native edit/validate. Commit the intended source and evidence so review binds an exact head. Obtain independent review at that exact revision; resolve actionable findings and renew proof/review after source changes.

Record real review evidence and a TypedReviewReceipt with separate implementer/reviewer identities and actual reviewed_revision/expected_head_sha. Use the review-digest helper for its payload digest. A generated receipt or review_present true does not perform the review. Native review currently checks a narrower planning contract; independent review remains an operator policy requirement.

3 IMPLEMENT AND REVIEW.code:
csdlc review --request review-request.json
csdlc review --request review-dispatch.json --execute

3 IMPLEMENT AND REVIEW: review-request.json is RemoteRouteRequest with issue/repository/implementer/reviewer/review_revision/expected_head_sha; review-dispatch.json wraps it in operation.kind review, canonical selector digest and exact_review_sha. Require ready in the result and valid current authority. Keep the typed receipt and actual evidence under .csdlc/evidence/ISSUE/.
4 CREATE AND VERIFY THE PR: Prepare a reviewed closing PR body containing exactly Closes #ISSUE, correct base and branch head. A checkpoint uses Part of #ISSUE and cannot terminally finish. Push the reviewed branch to its intended remote after verifying scope, then execute the native github-pr pull_request_create dispatch. Ordinary Git push transports the branch; it is not a raw GitHub lifecycle write.

4 CREATE AND VERIFY THE PR.code:
git push -u origin YOUR_REVIEWED_BRANCH
csdlc github-pr --request pr-create-dispatch.json --execute
csdlc pr-state --request remote-request.json --observe-github
csdlc publish --request remote-request.json --observe-github

4 CREATE AND VERIFY THE PR: The create dispatch's exact_review_sha and nested expected_head_sha match the reviewed head; mutation has action pull_request_create, base, head, title, body and draft. Retain the returned assigned numeric PR and authenticated mutation receipt. Verify actual base/head and closing linkage immediately.

Update RemoteRouteRequest with assigned PR/title/body, current head, mode closing, review_present, distinct principals and typed receipt path/digest. --observe-github obtains authenticated readback. The current publish route requires an existing authenticated PR readback, so its complete ready check occurs after actual PR creation. A pre-creation publish plan lacking readback must remain blocked; never forge receipts to get a green preflight. Native review and independent exact-head review precede the creation.

To transition from draft after required proof, use github-pr with pull_request_ready. Updating a PR title/body uses pull_request_update. Recheck publication after any material change. A published PR remains open/unmerged until explicit merge succeeds.
5 MERGE ONLY WITH AUTHORIZATION: Confirm required checks actually pass, unresolved review threads are resolved, current review is exact and the operator authorized this numeric PR merge. Use mutation pull_request_merge only through github-pr with explicit base, method merge and current review receipt path/digest. Put the actual authorization reference in operator_approval; text alone is not approval.

Retain authenticated reconciliation. Unsupported branch policy, incomplete observations or head/base/check drift stay blocked. All retries after merge intent are observation-only; do not delete the guard or send a second raw merge.
6 FINISH: Use TerminalRouteRequest repository/issue/numeric PR/expected_head_sha/mode closing and credential_names. To persist terminal truth include terminal_state with actual reconciliation root and exact canonical state/receipt locations from csdlc(1). Linked: .csdlc/v3/issues/ISSUE/terminal.json and .csdlc/evidence/ISSUE/terminal-receipt.json. Primary: resolved Git metadata csdlc-v3/local/v3/issues/ISSUE/terminal.json and csdlc-v3/local/evidence/ISSUE/terminal-receipt.json.

Finish independently observes merged PR, correct expected head and closed linked issue; no second GitHub mutation or closeout PR is needed. Retain returned terminal state/receipt and distinguish terminal observation from persistence when terminal_state is omitted.

7 CLEAN.code:
csdlc clean --request cleanup-preview.json
csdlc clean --request cleanup-remove.json

7 CLEAN: Before cleaning from primary, repeat the authenticated finish invocation from primary with terminal_state.repository_root set to that primary checkout and primary canonical Git-metadata state/receipt paths. The linked finish receipt in step 6 is not a primary cleanup receipt: do not copy it or point primary cleanup at the linked .csdlc file. Retain the newly authenticated primary receipt and its byte digest.

Run clean from the primary, not the target you will remove. Supply the actual approved parent, primary repository root, exact registered candidate, expected head and that primary durable terminal receipt path/digest. First remove false; only a Removable result supplies the preview receipt for a second request with remove true and matching preview_receipt_digest.

Preserve dirty, live or unregistered work. The cleanup gate checks a live-worktree marker and Git state; it is not a general host process scanner. Remove only the exact target and verify the returned Removed result. Do not broaden cleanup to other issue worktrees.
RECOVERY: Local compare-and-swap drift: inspect actual current state and regenerate only the intended semantic edit with fresh digest. Interrupted transaction: retain original request and state, use the identical native mutator request, and route unresolved failures to bounded tooling repair. No handwritten index/journal recovery.

Remote uncertain response: same exact request, same target and retained intent; native reconciliation observes the remote effect. An uncertain result is not a successful publication, merge or finish. Read csdlc-github-pr(1) for merge-specific one-shot dispatch semantics.
This manual's schema fixtures prove request shape and selected guard/plan behavior. They do not claim an end-to-end live GitHub deployment or authorize example targets.
